# Convert IMD into a categorical factor with 'Quintile 5' as the reference
main_dataset$imd_quintile <- factor(main_dataset$imd_quintile, 
                                    levels = c("5", "4", "3", "2", "1"))

# Verify the structure alongside your other categorical metrics
str(main_dataset$imd_quintile)


library(lcmm)

m3_with_imd <- Jointlcmm(
  fixed = eGFR ~ observation_time, 
  mixture = ~ observation_time,
  random = ~ observation_time, 
  subject = "patient_id",
  
  # Latent class membership predictors including socioeconomic status (IMD)
  classmb = ~ baseline_mental_health + baseline_bp + baseline_dm + imd_quintile,
  
  survival = Surv(time, status) ~ mixture(cohort), 
  hazard = "3-quant-splines",
  hazardtype = "CompetingRisks",
  
  data = main_dataset, 
  ng = 3, 
  B = m1 # Initial parameters vector
)



# 1. Extract coefficients and standard errors
estimates <- m3_with_imd$best
se <- sqrt(diag(m3_with_imd$V))

# 2. Isolate rows corresponding to class membership
mb_rows <- grep("classmb", names(estimates))

# 3. Compile clean, interpretable Odds Ratios
or_table_full <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(estimates)[mb_rows],
  Odds_Ratio = exp(estimates[mb_rows]),
  Lower_95_CI = exp(estimates[mb_rows] - 1.96 * se[mb_rows]),
  Upper_95_CI = exp(estimates[mb_rows] + 1.96 * se[mb_rows]),
  p_value = 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(estimates[mb_rows] / se[mb_rows])))
)

# Print results rounded to 3 decimal places
print(round(or_table_full[, 2:5], 3))



#add mental health
library(lcmm)

m3_interaction <- Jointlcmm(
  fixed = eGFR ~ observation_time, 
  mixture = ~ observation_time,
  random = ~ observation_time, 
  subject = "patient_id",
  
  # 'classmb' now includes the multi-level categorical interaction effect
  classmb = ~ baseline_bp + baseline_dm + baseline_mental_health * imd_quintile,
  
  survival = Surv(time, status) ~ mixture(cohort), 
  hazard = "3-quant-splines",
  hazardtype = "CompetingRisks",
  
  data = main_dataset, 
  ng = 3, 
  B = m1 # Vector of initial values from 1-class model
)

# View the full output parameters
summary(m3_interaction)


# 1. Extract parameters and standard errors
estimates <- m3_interaction$best
se <- sqrt(diag(m3_interaction$V))

# 2. Match all rows belonging to the class membership sub-model
mb_rows <- grep("classmb", names(estimates))

# 3. Create a clean results table
interaction_or_table <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(estimates)[mb_rows],
  Odds_Ratio = exp(estimates[mb_rows]),
  Lower_95_CI = exp(estimates[mb_rows] - 1.96 * se[mb_rows]),
  Upper_95_CI = exp(estimates[mb_rows] + 1.96 * se[mb_rows]),
  p_value = 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(estimates[mb_rows] / se[mb_rows])))
)

# View the table
print(round(interaction_or_table[, 2:5], 3))


# Test if the interaction block as a whole is statistically significant
# Identify the indices of the interaction terms within your model coefficients
interaction_indices <- grep("baseline_mental_health.*:imd_quintile", names(m3_interaction$best))

# Run the multivariate Wald test
wald_result <- WaldMult(m3_interaction, pos = interaction_indices)
print(wald_result)
